evidence: Caes. BG 7.46: oppidī mūrus ab plānitiē rēctā regiōne, sī nūllus ānfrāctus intercēderet, MCC passūs aberat (Lewis & Short s.v. regiō)

terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase, “in a running measurement”; not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections. Caesar’s rēctā regiōne is the classical way to give a distance in a straight line.
terms.gloss: as the crow flies (literally “by a running measure”)

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Lewis & Short: regio
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
